title: Norway’s Mortgage Risk Is Moving Towards the Boundary
trigger: Finanstilsynet published its 2026 mortgage lending survey on 29 October. The weighted average debt-to-income ratio rose to 333% from 329% in 2025, while first-time buyers’ average LTV rose to 79% from 77%.
limitations: Survey of approximately 12,000 new loans from 25 banks, not a full mortgage stock. Observed averages describe different cohorts. The model applies hypothetical LTV and price shocks to a single property; it is not an estimate of bank losses, PD or LGD.
formula: Loan = home value × origination LTV. Stressed collateral value = home value × (1 − price decline). Equity buffer = stressed collateral value − loan. Stressed LTV = loan / stressed collateral value. No amortisation, recovery costs or borrower cash flow are modelled.
decision: Use origination LTV bands and stressed collateral buffers jointly, rather than relying on the average debt-to-income ratio alone. Validate results with loan-level affordability, guarantees and geographic exposures.
worked_example: Illustrative worked example: a NOK 5.0m home financed at 79% LTV carries NOK 3.95m of debt. A 20% price decline leaves NOK 50,000 collateral equity and produces a 98.75% stressed LTV.
